notes_for_editor: Thin record: one row in the tnlandforms Georgia list. The elevation column has no unit (70 read as feet gives 21.3 m in the record). The codes BLL-65191 and gfc-840 are not explained on any crawled page, so the story does not interpret them. The list's header says names for towers 73 and above are the compiler's own, so 'brantley' matches the county name and may not be a historical name. Two web searches found no history for this tower. The NHLR Georgia list, the FFLOS Georgia cache and the Eastern U.S. Lookouts Georgia list contain no Brantley tower. A 2026 fire in Brantley County (the Highway 82 Fire, 22,419 acres, 110 homes destroyed, per WTOC at https://www.wtoc.com/2026/06/11/full-account-highway-82-fire-historic-destruction-massive-response-detailed-by-state-officials/) is county-level. No source links it to this tower, so the story leaves it out. An editor who can place the tower relative to the burn area could decide whether it belongs in the story. The story is 137 words, above the 120-word floor.
